daily.title: GST Demand Cannot Be Sustained Solely on GSTR-9C and VAT Return Mismatch: GSTAT Patna
daily.summary: GSTAT Patna sets aside Rs.36.59 lakh demand based on GSTR-9C and VAT return mismatch, holding that taxable supply must be established, and orders remand. Summary: The Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT), State Bench Patna, Division Bench Court No. II, held that a mere arithmetical difference between turnover disclosed in GSTR-9C and a VAT return cannot independently establish liability under GST. The Tribunal set aside the demand of Rs.36,59,726, comprising tax of Rs.17,59,576, interest of Rs.17,24,192 and penalty of Rs.1,75,958, raised against Medicare Environmental Management Private Limited, and remanded the matter to the original adjudicating authority for fresh adjudication…

daily.title: SGST Officers Cannot Proceed Against Out-of-State Taxpayer Without Temporary ID: GSTAT Thiruvananthapuram
daily.summary: GSTAT quashes Rs.75.20 lakh confiscation order for lack of territorial jurisdiction and failure to specify the applicable clause of Section 130(1). Summary: The Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT), Thiruvananthapuram, Division Bench Court No. I, held that the State GST officers of Keralam could not have exercised jurisdiction over a taxpayer registered in Andhra Pradesh without issuing a temporary identification number in respect of transactions allegedly undertaken in Keralam. The Tribunal further held that confiscation proceedings under Section 130(1) of the CGST/KGST Act could not be initiated without specifying the particular clause alleged to have been contravened.

daily.title: GST Penalty Unsustainable for E-Way Bill Technical Glitch Without Intent to Evade Tax: GSTAT Bengaluru
daily.summary: GSTAT Bengaluru quashes Rs.76,206 penalty for an e-way bill software glitch without tax evasion intent and directs refund with statutory interest. Summary: The Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT), State Bench Bengaluru, Division Bench Court II, held that a discrepancy in the place of dispatch mentioned in an e-way bill arising from a software integration glitch, without evidence of intention to evade tax, did not justify invocation of Section 129 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 .

daily.title: Senior Citizen Tax Rates For Tax Year 2026-27: With Example on Different Income Levels
daily.summary: Senior citizens in India can pay tax under two systems: the New Regime and the Old Regime.For Tax Year 2026–27, the New Regime has the same slabs for ever This guide compares the two in simple steps, so you can pick the one that saves you more tax. Tax Year 2026–27 is the same period as FY 2026–27 (AY 2027–28) under the older terminology. Tax is progressive, so each rate applies only to the income inside its band. A 4% Health and Education Cess is added on top, and a surcharge applies at higher incomes.

daily.title: 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves: April – September 2026
daily.summary: It may be recalled that in February 2004 , the Reserve Bank initiated the practice of compiling half-yearly reports on the management of foreign exchange reserves and making them public to promote greater transparency and enhance disclosure in the management of the country’s foreign exchange reserves. In this connection, Reserve Bank of India has today released the 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves with reference to end-September 2026. During April-September 2026, India’s foreign exchange reserves increased from US$ 691.11 billion to US$ 737.78 billion.

breaking.summary: The central bank accepted offers aggregating ₹8,002.80 crore and issued destination securities (SGS’) aggregating ₹8,261.548 crore. Under conversion auction, near-maturity SGS’ (source securities) are simultaneously exchanged for longer-maturity SGS’ (destination securities). This is aimed at reducing the redemption pressure on the states, increase the maturity profile of borrowings and consolidate debt. While in the case of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu, SGS’ offered by market participants was either equal or higher than the notified amount for the respective securities, in the case of poll bound Punjab, the SGS’ offered was less than the notified amount.
